An estimate of 25+ personnel would be required to permit 2 shift operation of such a facility. This includes the following estimate: 2 shop managers; 2 senior CAM programmers; 2 manufacturing engineers/schedulers; 6-8 machine operators; 8 Q/A staff including CMM programmers, document control, CMM operators; 2 facilities maintenance personnel and 4 administrative staff to cover roles such as purchasing/receiving, inventory management, ES&H, HR, accounting and executive leadership. The above assumes a stand alone facility and some of the above could be shared with other operations, such as chemistry, welding, RF validation to drive down some of the Q/A and administrative payroll. Further if managed as an expansion of an existing industry shop, many of the higher level technical staff could be shared among other business activities thus providing significant cost savings. Page 13 of 55 “Manufacturing full-scale high gradient copper accelerators: Electron beam welding and allied processes” Prepared for the U.S. Department of Energy ARDAP program The monthly payroll costs would vary by location and where in the production lifecycle we are. For example, early in the development cycle, higher value staffing is required in order to establish production plans, perform facilities layout, establish CAM and CMM programs, design fixtures, develop Q/A documentation and debug processes. In the later stages of production, the staffing levels would shift toward operators and lower value labor executing the previously developed plans and procedures at scale. Further, as this would be seen as a temporary position, even if in operation for approximately 4-6 years, a higher wage premium will be required for some positions such as shop and Q/A management, lead machinists/programmers and engineers. In high cost of living regions such as Los Angeles or the Bay area, the average wage could easily be in the $60/hr level during initial setup periods but drop to the $40/hr level once in production. If such a facility was operating under the umbrella of a federal contract, the payroll calculations must also include expenses such as benefits, overhead, G/A and fees, which for an average facility could be considered at an approximately 2x multiplier on top of the wage. This would amount to a rough estimate of $540k/month to $360k/month payroll. Staffing levels would also have to consider attrition, and have a mixture of staffing overage for redundancy in critical positions and access to temporary labor pools for more easily replaceable positions such as operators, maintenance and some admin. These factors will add approximately 5-15% to the above numbers, and are also highly dependent on the schedule risk tolerance of the project.
